teams.heading: Jake White names four uncapped players in first Fiji squad
teams.body: Jake White's first Fiji squad, named ahead of Saturday's 34-28 win over Japan in Tokyo, included four uncapped players. Nacani Boginisoko and Aporosa Vuniyayawa started, while Peni Naruma and Kavekini Boselawa were named among the replacements. White picked no Europe-based players for the match, and said the calibre of player picked from the islands could make Fiji a force at next year's World Cup.

lead.why: It is the team's own Test squad news, sourced in full, and the only shortlist item that is not a repeat of the Japan result or the Nawaqanitawase story.

teams.heading: Jack van Poortvliet signs new Leicester Tigers deal as England's 27-cap scrum-half
teams.body: Jack van Poortvliet has committed his future to Leicester Tigers, the club he grew up supporting. The Tigers vice-captain has made 118 appearances since his 2019 debut and was part of the 2021-22 squad that won the Gallagher PREM. The 27-cap England international has also earned an Elite Player Squad contract for 2026-27. He added: "It was a pretty easy decision to stay. I love it here and long may that continue."

lead.why: It is the only new England men's item that is not already run, club-match or women's coverage.

teams.heading: French rugby observes minute's applause for 17-year-old Cléa Menier this weekend
teams.body: Cléa Menier, a 17-year-old back row for Union du Bassin Marmandais, died in hospital after what her club called an "accident" in an amateur under-18s match against Agen Agglo Rugby on Saturday. The French Rugby Federation says a minute's applause will be held before every professional and amateur match in France this weekend, and that the tribute is agreed with her family. Neither the club nor the federation has disclosed the nature of her injury.

lead.why: The Menier death is the most widely covered French rugby story in today's pack, and the federation's weekend tribute reaches every French pitch, so it is the one a fan would raise with a mate.

teams.heading: Stuart McCloskey bundles over for try in Ulster's 34-26 defeat to Bulls
teams.body: Ulster's 34-26 defeat at Loftus Versfeld was a day for Stuart McCloskey to make his case. The centre assisted one try and then bundled over for another to get Ulster within striking distance, and Planet Rugby rated him 8. Its writer calls it a 'statement performance' that will put Andy Farrell on notice just before the Nations Championship. The piece says he 'was aggressive and physical in contact' throughout.

lead.why: The only new men's item in the pack that bears on Ireland's Test selection, with McCloskey's form tied directly to Farrell before the Nations Championship.

teams.heading: Italy have conceded 131 points in three games, including 10-57 to Australia
teams.body: Italy's points record is the story the table tells most bluntly. Across their three games so far they have scored 37 points and conceded 131, a points difference of -94. The most recent of those, a 10-57 loss to Australia in Round three, accounts for the largest single share of that total. Their next match is Round four against South Africa, the side who beat them 32-14 at home in November 2025, and the log leaves little room for comfort.

teams.heading: Tom English says Darcy Graham is working back into Scotland's wing picture
teams.body: Darcy Graham is working back into contention, but Tom English's BBC Sport reader Q&A this week points to a hard choice in Scotland's back three. English says Jamie Dobie and Kyle Steyn are the two most consistent wings right now, with Kyle Rowe an inch away, and sees obvious logic in Dobie covering two positions from the bench. That would leave Graham outside the 23, which English describes as a hard call.

lead.why: The only shortlist item that is Scotland squad selection analysis and not already covered in today's squad-depth edition.

teams.heading: Macs Page taken off on oxygen after head hit against Stormers
teams.body: Scarlets winger Macs Page, uncapped and left out of Steve Tandy's 39-man autumn squad, was forced off in Cape Town after his head hit the turf in the United Rugby Championship clash with the Stormers. He appeared to lose consciousness as he spilled the ball forward, and a stretcher was brought on before he walked off on oxygen. Page had already dotted down for his fifth try of the season. Scarlets' Nigel Davies had said it was only a matter of time before Wales brought him in.

lead.why: A fresh Wales-eligible selection storyline and a head-injury scare for an uncapped prospect Tandy left out of the autumn squad, which is more newsworthy than the already-run Faletau and Freddie Thomas

teams.heading: Sam Prendergast a doubt with wrist injury for Pumas' Ireland test
teams.body: Ireland's fly-half picture for November remains unclear. RTÉ Sport reported on 24 October that Sam Prendergast's wrist injury makes him a doubt, and The Sun described a major injury scare. No fitness update has surfaced in today's coverage, so the Pumas head into their London camp without knowing whether Prendergast will start at No. 10 for Ireland.

teams.heading: Wallabies flanker Rob Leota signs with Clermont until January 2027
teams.body: Rob Leota, the 21-cap Wallabies flanker, has signed for Clermont, committing until January 2027 after leaving Bayonne as a free agent. Urios said: "It's always difficult to find an additional player at this time of year." The 29-year-old is a powerful ball carrier for an Auvergne side awaiting the return of several injured players, and he was not among the 33 Les Kiss named for the spring tour.

lead.why: The only NEW item on the shortlist, and it is a Wallabies flanker's move rather than a story already run.

teams.heading: Japan score 327 points and concede 301 in last 11 Tests
teams.body: Across their last 11 games, Japan have scored 327 points and conceded 301, averages of 29.7 and 27.4 a game. Their biggest win in that window was a 63-14 home victory over USA in September 2026, in the Pacific Nations Cup Knockout Stage. Their next fixture is Wales in Round 4. Those numbers give a plain picture of the form Japan take into it.

teams.heading: Richie Mo’unga not yet ruled out of Europe tour with calf tear
teams.body: Richie Mo’unga has not yet been ruled out of the Europe tour, a rare bit of good news after a triple injury blow that also cost Shannon Frizell, Tyrel Lomax and Samisoni Taukei’aho their places. The flyhalf missed both Bledisloe Cup Tests against Australia with a calf tear, and the All Blacks face Scotland, England and Wales before the finals weekend at Twickenham.

lead.why: Mo’unga's status is the one item in the Test-squad injury report that has not already been run, and it is the only possible positive in it.

teams.heading: Springboks' eight defeats since 2023 read like a manual for beating them
teams.body: Planet Rugby's analysis argues South Africa's eight Test defeats since the start of 2023 read like a coaching manual for beating the world champions. The winning side averaged 29.9 points across the eight, and none of them scored fewer tries than the Springboks did, so scoring capacity is the first thing the evidence asks for. The Springboks face Italy, France and Ireland in the November leg of the Nations Championship.

lead.why: The only shortlist item about the men's Test side; the others are women's WXV, club matches, or a story already run.
